subject: Post-demo recap: Context & token economics — next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@cartiq.com>, Samir Patel <samir@cartiq.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap: Context & token economics — next steps

Hi Emily / Samir,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed set of next steps so we can align pricing to your expected token profile. I captured the explicit signal you gave on volumes and context needs and added a recommended pricing vector for the next-stage POC.

Quick recap from our call:
- Primary use case: contextual product recommendations and conversational support embedded in web/mobile (search + follow-ups).
- Expected Q4 POC traffic: ~8M API requests/month with an average of 1.2 prompts per request (includes follow-ups).
- Sample prompt depth observed in your examples: 150–300 tokens (average prompt tokens we saw ~220).
- Expected completion length: 300–900 tokens depending on whether the flow includes multi-step reasoning (sample avg completion tokens ~520).
- Context window needs: most flows fit within 8k, but you flagged two features requiring longer histories (30% of sessions need 32k; rare enterprise analytics flows 5% need 128k).

High-level token mix estimate (from the sample set you shared):
- Avg prompt tokens: 220 tokens
- Avg completion tokens: 520 tokens
- Token distribution: ~72% sessions within 8k, ~23% within 32k, ~5% require 128k.

Target unit-econ ask from you: target $/1M tokens to budget for the POC. Based on the above, we propose a pricing range and configuration that balances latency and cost: 

Redwood suggested POC economics (composable):
- Target list price (public-hosted style) : $120 / 1M tokens (starting point)
- POC committed unit economics (volume + 12-week commit): $95–110 / 1M tokens depending on routing to quantized variants + batch settings
- Expected raw infra token cost (approx): $22–28 / 1M tokens (varies by model quantization and context length mix)
- Target gross margin to expect in a Dedicated deal: ~65–75% (after infra and operations).

Recommendations to hit the $95–110 / 1M target:
- Route 70–75% of calls to a 8k-optimized variant (q4 quant), enable prefix caching for common prompts.
- For the 32k cohort, use our mid-tier model with adaptive batching and a 2x higher per-token price tier.
- Reserve fallback policy: if 128k requests spike, route to a longer-context variant with rotation and shed non-critical background workloads.

Attachments included: MAP_Cartiq_2028.xlsx (mutual action plan template), token_mix_samples.txt (sample token counts), RFI_SOC2_answer.pdf (requested security answers).

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm the monthly token volume band you want us to price against (pick one: 250M, 500M, 1B tokens).
2) We will produce a targeted POC quote with an explicit $/1M figure and a recommended routing policy and model mix.
3) Sign MAP and kick off a 6-week POC (we'll scope dedicated monitoring + eval prompts).

Can you confirm which token volume bucket you want priced and whether Cartiq is comfortable with an initial 12-week commit for the POC?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if helpful.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
M: +1 (415) 555-0199

---
Redwood Inference | reliable low-latency inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
From: Emily Zhao <emily@cartiq.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@cartiq.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Context & token economics — next steps

Diego — thanks for the thorough write-up, this is super helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) Volume: for the POC we expect closer to the 500M token band (ballpark across prompts + completions). We'll provide a 1-week sampling of production logs to validate.
2) Token mix: the 5% 128k flows are indeed small but critical (those are our analytics exports that must keep full history). The 32k use is more common in the onboarding flows (roughly 20–25%).
3) Target price: Emily (exec) asked me to push for a target <= $100 / 1M at POC scale. She knows there will be variance for longer contexts.

We can sign the MAP as long as the POC quote includes: a) explicit per-context tier pricing (8k / 32k / 128k), b) an SLA on 95th percentile latency for 8k flows, and c) clear observability for token-level billing.

I'll loop our procurement person if we get to commit. For now, please send the POC quote at the 500M bucket and show two scenarios: (1) fully-hosted list price, (2) committed POC price with the $/1M target you propose.

Thanks,
Emily
Head of Product, Cartiq

Emily — perfect, thanks for the clarity. I'll produce two scenarios for the 500M bucket and include explicit per-context-tier pricing as you requested. Draft outline below — I'll attach the quote and the MAP later today.

Scenario A (Hosted list):
- 8k tier: $130 / 1M tokens
- 32k tier: $320 / 1M tokens
- 128k tier: $1,100 / 1M tokens
- Observable token-level billing and per-route latency dashboards (default retention 90 days).

Scenario B (Committed POC, 12-week, 500M bucket):
- 8k tier: $98 / 1M tokens
- 32k tier: $245 / 1M tokens
- 128k tier: $900 / 1M tokens
- Includes: prefix KV caching for onboarding flows, a small dedicated capacity reservation to stabilize 95th percentile for 8k flows, and a joint eval plan.

Notes on assumptions: average prompt/completion mix from your samples (prompt 220 tokens / completion 520 tokens). If the completion tail skews higher (+30%), the POC price for 32k/128k will need to be revisited.

I'll attach MAP_Cartiq_2028.xlsx and token_mix_samples.txt in the next email and submit the formal quote through HubSpot. If Marion from procurement needs an initial SOW language, we can provide a one-paragraph SOW for the MAP.

Would Tuesday morning next week for a short pricing review call work for you?

Best,
Diego

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: Cartiq pricing notes

Diego / Marissa — copying internal notes for the quote preparation:
- Use 65% gross margin model when finalizing committed POC numbers; that lands the 8k at ~$98 and keeps room for support credits.
- Ensure MAP includes a clause for model variant pinning and rollback to smaller-context variant.
- Add a usage-based auto-scaling cap guard to avoid overrun during analytics exports (128k flows).
- I'll prepare a quick cost sensitivity table (vary completion token mean from 400 -> 700) and attach to the quote.

Karthik
Director, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
